about: Donnafugata was founded in 1983 by Giacomo Rallo, of a Marsala wine family with more than 170 years in the trade, and his wife Gabriella, a pioneer for women in Sicilian viticulture. Their children, José and Antonio, now run it, with estates at Contessa Entellina, on the volcanic island of Pantelleria and in Vittoria. In 2016 they realised their father’s long-held wish to work on Etna, Europe’s highest active volcano, planting a cellar in contrada Statella near Randazzo on the mountain’s northern slope.

Sul Vulcano comes from vineyards in six contrade between Randazzo and Castiglione di Sicilia, at 700 to 750 metres, on sandy soils formed from ancient lava flows. Some vines grow as traditional free-standing alberello on dry-stone terraces. Nerello Mascalese is picked by hand in October, fermented in stainless steel with eight to ten days on the skins, then aged 14 months, partly in tank and partly in used French barriques, followed by at least seven months in bottle. The label, by longtime Donnafugata artist Stefano Vitale, shows a volcano goddess for the mountain locals simply call “a Muntagna.”

The producer describes a light ruby wine with wild berries, flowers and gentle spice, and present but well-integrated tannins with marked minerality. Falstaff’s tasters found cherry, raspberry and a hint of star anise in the 2022, with fine tannins and lively acidity. Vinous called it juicy and energetic, with crisp red fruit over a mineral core.
facts: Six contrade on Etna’s north slope, 730–750 m, sandy volcanic soils
14 months in tank and used French barriques, then 7+ months in bottle
